The lesson is written: "Plant foot, striking surface and lean: what each one does to a penalty kick", 30 minutes, objective O2. A short quiz on it is ready whenever you want it, and you can ask me anything about the lesson in the chat.

I could not read two of the academic sources in full. Two papers were blocked and two PDFs came back unreadable. The lesson therefore rests mainly on four coaching articles. The only study it cites is an abstract-level record: side-foot kicks were more accurate than instep kicks, and the error spread grew with ball speed. The lesson says all this. It also says that nothing it read measures the power gap between laces and inside-of-foot. It asks you to check that on your own video.

The lesson covers four inputs and what each does to accuracy, power and height:
- **Plant foot:** beside the ball keeps the ball low. Behind the ball makes the foot rise at contact and lifts the ball, which is the cause of the shots you send over the bar.
- **Contact point on the ball:** hitting below the centre lifts the ball. A simple height model, ignoring drag and spin, puts the limit at about 17 degrees for a 25 m/s ball from 11 m.
- **Striking surface:** laces give more power and a wider error spread. The inside of the foot gives a tighter spread. A 3-degree error misses a corner target by 0.58 m.
- **Lean:** mostly a sign of where the plant foot is, not a separate control.

It includes worked examples, practice items with answers and a daylight drill using a cone. Before you start it asks for the results of your last 10 penalties (scored, saved, wide, over the bar), because the practice section reuses them. Could you send those?

I also added a one-page diagnosis cheat sheet, a sources list and updated your notes.
